capabilities: capability privacy context cost latency and concurrency admission filters
deterministic preference health cache locality latency cost and load scoring
immutable-snapshot route-plan cache with health-generation invalidation

research_inputs.finding: vLLM Production Stack documents multimodel, model-aware and prefix-aware routing, observability, fast bootstrapping, and KV-cache offloading.
research_inputs.used_for: model-aware routing and cache/locality scoring as provider-neutral control-plane inputs

research_inputs.finding: LiteLLM documents unified multi-provider access, routing, load balancing, fallbacks, budgets, and user/team controls.
research_inputs.used_for: provider-neutral fallback planning and caller-supplied policy boundaries

research_inputs.finding: Ray Serve documents model-ID-aware routing over shared replicas, LRU model placement, and fallback when matching replicas are unavailable.
research_inputs.used_for: cache-hit preference, bounded route caching, and generation-aware snapshot replacement

research_inputs.finding: vLLM warns that distributed and KV-cache communications are insecure by default, API-key coverage is incomplete, and reverse-proxy allowlists and resource limits are required.
research_inputs.used_for: keeping routing separate from execution/network authorization and preserving fail-closed boundaries

limitations: The module plans routes but never calls a provider or inference engine.
Health values are caller-observed snapshots and are not independent attestation.
The benchmark is local control-plane overhead, not model quality, tokens per second, network latency, accelerator utilization, or production cost.
The cache is an in-process optimization keyed by immutable endpoint/request snapshot identity; distributed cache coherence is out of scope.
No physical GPU/NPU or external provider qualification is implied.
This upgrade does not claim AGI, model superiority, learning, model retraining, or production approval.
